gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the LAMTTO DC25's higher-resolution mode is a trade and not an upgrade: LAMTTO's own example is 2.5K + 720p + 720p + 1080p, so raising one camera above 1080p drops two others to 720p, and the camera takes at most a 128 GB card.
standout_why: I opened three results: milewitness.com and truepicked.com name no 4-channel camera at all (their highest is three channels), and dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam gives per-channel resolution for the Rexing C4, R4 and Botslab G980H but no frame rates and does not cover LAMTTO. ChatGPT's own answer said the DC25 has 'selectable higher-resolution modes' without saying those modes cut other channels to 720p. The other 11 results were not opened; their titles are 2-channel or general under-$200 lists. Rexing's and Botslab's stores returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so the finding rests on LAMTTO's pages only, which is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: A shopper cannot buy the DC25 at $149.99 expecting a sharper front view on top of four 1080p views: on LAMTTO's own wording it is either four 1080p channels or a mix with 720p channels. That makes the fair comparison under $200 four 1080p channels (LAMTTO DC25, LAMTTO DC21, and the Rexing C4 per Dealectric's existing page) against the Botslab G980H, which Dealectric's record lists at 3K front plus three 1080p views all at 25 fps for $192.70 through the link with code AA18. I could not re-read Botslab's page today. The DC21 is also a different layout: LAMTTO describes its side views as 'left and right cabin', so the page should say what each camera sees before ranking it for side-swipe coverage. Parking mode on both LAMTTO models needs the ACC hardwire kit, which LAMTTO says is in the box.
